dod_intent_evidence: Army SBIR Phase II 2022 ($1.6M) for the Automated Inventory Management System (AIMS) with their own abstract promising Nett Warrior/ATAK/CAMS compatibility and field deployment — SBIR record section.
score_evidence: "AI Camera Software: Reduce False Positives By 95%+" and "user-friendly Cloud platform offers seamless integration" → lab_language_intensity: accuracy-percent and cloud-native bragging with zero operational framing on the entire site
Only open role: "Sales Development Representative (Bellevue)" → hiring_profile_skew: zero field, deployment, or compliance roles four years after a Phase II that promised field testing

Abstract: "make AIMS fully compatible with Nett Warrior mobile devices and apps such as Android Team Awareness Kit (ATAK)" → deployment_awareness_absence kept mid-range; the defense abstract is ecosystem-fluent even though the commercial site is cloud-only
Phase II awarded 2022; no follow-on defense news since → stage_pressure: the transition window on AIMS has largely lapsed with the company's public energy on commercial security

blind_spots.blind_spot: The company's entire delivery architecture is a cloud SaaS, while AIMS must run at ammunition transfer points where the abstract's own premise is minimizing time stationary under enemy threat — a DDIL environment with no cloud reachback
blind_spots.operator_reality: An E-5 running resupply at an ATP with jammed or absent comms cannot stream video to a cloud inference service; the munitions count has to happen on the Nett Warrior end-user device or it does not happen
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: All commercial revenue comes from monitoring centers with broadband; every engineering incentive since 2022 has pushed toward the cloud platform, not edge inference
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Our user-friendly Cloud platform offers seamless integration with existing systems, enabling security providers to enhance responsiveness without costly on-site hardware upgrades

blind_spots.blind_spot: Phase II promised field testing and deployment on Army networks, but the company shows no ATO/RMF/IL or CMMC language anywhere and is hiring nobody who would own accreditation
blind_spots.operator_reality: Camera-based AI touching Form 581 munitions records on Nett Warrior needs RMF accreditation and an ATO sponsor; without one, AIMS stays a demo no unit is allowed to plug in
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: Their compliance world is commercial alarm-industry standards; the one open req is a sales SDR, so no ISSO or deployment engineer exists to carry the paperwork
blind_spots.evidence_quote: This will make AIMS available for field testing and deployment, in every kind of theater

blind_spots.blind_spot: The 2022 abstract names the right integrations (ATAK, CAMS, Nett Warrior) but four years on there is no public evidence of a transition partner, follow-on award, or Army advocacy chain — operators counting ammo faster is not adoption
blind_spots.operator_reality: Without a PM-level champion and a funded transition vehicle, AIMS dies in the valley even if the field tests worked; the months-to-field now exceed any funded months remaining
blind_spots.why_likely_missing: The commercial security business ("Join Over 1000 Companies") pays the bills, so nobody at a 33-person company is working the DoD advocacy chain
blind_spots.evidence_quote: Actuate will streamline the User Interface (UI) issues and make AIMS fully compatible with Nett Warrior mobile devices

opener_hook: Actuate's 2022 Army Phase II promised AIMS field testing on Nett Warrior and ATAK; four years later the only open role on the books is a sales SDR in Bellevue.
what_they_do: Commercial AI video analytics for security monitoring centers, with a stalled Army Phase II product for computer-vision munitions inventory on Nett Warrior/ATAK.
